edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Adam protolapsus, ut Dei praecepta vitaret, Belias tentator fuit de invidia palmae; Contulit et nobis seu boni seu mali quod egit, Dux nati nativitatis, morimur indeque per illum: Ex divino ipse ut recedens exsul a verbo. Finitis sex millibus annis immortales erimus. Gustato pomi ligno mors intravit in orbem: Hoc ligno mortis generamur vitae futurae. In ligno pendet vita ferens poma, praecepta. Cavete nunc vitalia poma credentes. Lex a ligno data est homini primitivo timenda, Mors unde provenit neglecta lege primordi: Nunc extende manum, et sume de ligno vitali. Optima lex Domini sequens de ligno processit. Perdita lex prima; gustat unde licet illi. Qui deos adorat vetitos, mala gaudia vitae. Respuite gustum; sufficiet scire quod esset. Si vivere vultis, reddite vos legi secundae. Templorum culturas, daemonum fata vitate Vertite vos Christo, et eritis Deo sodales. Xanta Dei lex est, quae mortuos vivere docet. Imnum sibi solus Dominus proferre praecepit; Zabolicam legem omnes omnino vitate.
thought_title: Adam and the Tree of Life
pass_a_gloss: Adam first sinner, so that he might avoid God's commands, Belial was tempter because of envy of the palm; and he conferred on us what he did, either good or evil, Leader of the birth of birth, we die from that and through him: From the divine he himself receding, an exile from the word. When six thousand years are finished, we will be immortal. Death entered the world when the wood of the tree was tasted: By this wood of death we are born for future life. Life hangs on the tree bearing fruits, commands. Beware now, believers, of the life-giving fruits. The law was given to primitive man from the tree, to be feared, Death comes from neglect of the primal law: Now extend your hand, and take from the life-giving tree. The best law of the Lord follows, proceeding from the tree. The first law was lost; it is permitted to taste from that. He who worships forbidden gods, has evil joys of life. Reject the taste; it will suffice to know what it was. If you want to live, give yourselves back to the second law. Avoid the cults of temples, the fates of demons, Turn yourselves to Christ, and you will be companions of God. The law of God is Xanta, which teaches the dead to live. The Lord alone commanded to proclaim his name; completely avoid the law of Zabulon.
pass_b_english: Belial tempted Adam, the first sinner, out of envy for the palm, so that Adam would evade God's commands. What Adam did, whether good or evil, he passed on to us; he is the Leader of the birth of birth, and we die from that and through him. He himself receded from the divine, an exile from the Word. When six thousand years are finished, we will be immortal. Death entered the world when the tree's wood was tasted; by this wood of death we are born for future life. Life hangs on the tree bearing fruits and commands. Believers, beware now of the life-giving fruits. The law was given from the tree to primitive man, to be feared; death comes from neglect of the primal law. Now extend your hand and take from the life-giving tree. The best law of the Lord follows, proceeding from the tree. The first law was lost; it is permitted to taste from that tree. Whoever worships forbidden gods has evil joys of life. Reject the taste; it will suffice to know what it was. If you want to live, give yourselves back to the second law. Avoid the cults of temples and the fates of demons; turn yourselves to Christ, and you will be companions of God. The law of God is Xanta, which teaches the dead to live. The Lord alone commanded that his name be proclaimed; completely avoid the law of Zabulon.
